topline.text: Another quiet 24-48 hours - across DfE, Ofsted, safeguarding, funding and Sheffield/South Yorkshire sources, nothing new and properly corroborated cleared the bar, so today's edition runs short rather than padded.
Reminder, not new: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform now closes in two weeks, on 19 November.
Still on the radar: DfE's accredited statistics release for autumn-term 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions is due this month, with no exact day confirmed yet.

diary.text: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform (white paper proposals on internal suspension, reintegration and parental engagement) closes.
DfE due to publish autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics for England.

items.lede: Exclusion-reform call for evidence: two weeks left to respond.
items.body: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform - part of the 'Every child achieving and thriving' white paper - is seeking views from practitioners and researchers on proposals including wider use of internal suspension, reintegration support and parental engagement. It closes 19 November.
items.action: Worth a quick nudge to anyone on the inclusion team who wants input in before the window closes.

box.label: Jargon-buster - internal suspension
box.intro: Comes up throughout DfE's live exclusion-reform call for evidence.
box.text: Removing a pupil from their usual class or timetable for a fixed period while keeping them on the school site, supervised separately, rather than issuing a formal suspension. DfE is asking the sector whether wider, more consistent use of it could reduce reliance on off-site suspensions.
